sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Browser-only setup and imports
sections.what: Marks the page as browser code and imports the state helper used for form values.
sections.why: The page needs typing and button clicks, so it must run in the browser.

sections.name: AdminSetupPage (part 1)
sections.title: Form state and submit handling
sections.what: Holds the form values, the result message, and the busy state. On submit, sends the secret and password to the setup route and shows the reply.
sections.why: Shows the page is busy while waiting, then shows whatever the server returned.
sections.watch_out: The secret field uses password display, which hides typing on screen, but the value is still held in the page.

sections.name: AdminSetupPage (part 2)
sections.title: Setup screen layout
sections.what: Draws the page layout, the success and error banners, the secret and password fields, and the create button.
sections.why: The password must be at least 8 characters, which the browser checks before sending.
sections.watch_out: The length check here happens only in the browser. Whether the server also checks is not visible in this file.

summary: A one-time setup screen where the owner enters a setup secret and a password to create the admin account.
purpose: Lets the owner create the first admin login through the web page instead of a command line.
why: Likely reason: the setup secret lives in the hosting settings, so only someone with access to those settings can finish setup. The code does not state this.
how: Shows a form with the setup secret and a new password. On submit, sends both to the setup route and shows a success or error message. After success, shows a link to the login page.
inputs: The setup secret and the new password typed by the user.
outputs: A success message or an error message on screen.
risks: The success message has the owner's email address written into the page, so a change of owner email needs a code change. Whether setup can only run once is enforced by the server and is not visible here. The password is sent in the request body, which is only safe over an encrypted connection.
debug: If setup shows an error message, check the response from the setup route. If the message says Network error, the server could not be reached. Confirm the setup secret matches the hosting environment variable.
